recap.summary: Week 7 was an 80.90-114.62 loss to bsummy51 that dropped us to 1-6 and left us last in the league in points for. Three of the nine starting slots produced 0.0: Lamar Jackson (Out, ankle) at QB, Brian Thomas Jr. at WR1 while Jacksonville was on bye, and Cameron Dicker at K during the Chargers bye. Grading last week's packet: the two waiver claims it built the week around (Tanner McKee at QB, Chase McLaughlin at K) never landed in the app - the roster is unchanged - so the packet's entire contingency plan for the QB and K holes went unexecuted and we ate the zeros it explicitly warned about. Worse, Brian Thomas was left in the lineup on a bye the packet itself flagged as a bye, which is the second straight week a bye-week zero decided a game. The Josh Jacobs 'dead roster weight' call was flatly wrong: he posted 20.1 from the bench, more than any starter but Jameson Williams, and Justin Jefferson's 8.4 also sat. The calls that were right were the ceiling plays: Jameson Williams (26.1) and Luther Burden (23.7) were the top two scorers on the roster, exactly as projected, and RJ Harvey (14.0) was again the best RB. Waiver priority #1 is still in hand, which is the one asset that gives this week any leverage. Net: we lost a game we were never going to win, but we also gave away roughly 35 points of avoidable zeros for the third consecutive week. The structural fix for Week 8 is simple - every player in the starting nine this week has a game and no designation.
what_worked: Jameson Williams 26.1 - the ceiling-over-floor FLEX/WR call has now hit in back-to-back healthy weeks
Luther Burden III 23.7 - the 'he is a weekly starter, not a bye-week fill-in' call was correct and he locks into WR2
RJ Harvey 14.0 - third straight usable week; he stays in the starting backfield
Waiver priority #1 preserved - nothing in the pool was worth burning it on, and it is still available now
what_hurt: Brian Thomas Jr. started at WR1 on Jacksonville's bye for 0.0 - a pure roster-management zero, the same error as Jameson Williams in Week 6
Lamar Jackson started while Out for the third straight week (0.0) - Herbert was on bye so the slot was forced, but the McKee claim that was supposed to cover it was never submitted
Cameron Dicker 0.0 on the Chargers bye because the McLaughlin kicker add was never executed
Josh Jacobs 20.1 on the bench and Justin Jefferson 8.4 on the bench - the packet's read on Jacobs' role was wrong, and benching Jefferson was indefensible
recap.self_grade: D+ - correct on the ceiling plays (Williams, Burden, Harvey) and on protecting waiver priority, badly wrong on Jacobs, and the packet's contingency structure (claim McKee, claim a kicker, bench the bye players) failed at the execution layer and cost ~35 points of zeros.

He is the depth-1 tight end in Los Angeles catching passes from Herbert, has led the Chargers in receiving in a game this season, and runs a route share in the mid-60s. He is volatile (he has goose-egged on a sub-10% target share week), but there is no healthy alternative and the upside in a Herbert-led passing game is real.

He beats A.J. Brown (7.8 in his first full game back, still working into a role) and Brian Thomas Jr. (two 0.0s and a depth-3 listing) for this slot without much debate.

Back from the Chargers bye and one of the highest-volume, highest-accuracy kickers in the league in a scoring system that pays 4-5 points for 40+ yard field goals. Last week's 0.0 was the bye, not performance. No stream is better; hold him through Week 17.

I could not verify this week's specific game environment before my search budget ran out, so I am holding the known-productive unit rather than chasing the Jacksonville stream blind - see waivers for the conditional swap if you want the matchup play.

I could not re-verify his practice status this week (search budget exhausted); if he is a confirmed full participant with a normal route share and Jameson Williams picks up any designation, swap them.

Two 0.0s plus a depth-3 listing in a crowded Jacksonville receiver room is not a startable profile right now, and the talent case for holding him is a dynasty argument, not a Week 8 argument. He is trade capital in the mrkw offer; if he is not moved and posts another dud, he becomes the drop for the next trending add.

DROP - the designated cut for the Dylan Sampson claim. Buried behind Omarion Hampton in Los Angeles, 0.4 points the last time he touched the field, and he occupies a bench spot we need for a back who can actually start during the Week 10-11 bye gauntlet.

IR DESIGNATION - CHECK THE APP FIRST. He is fourth/fifth in Philadelphia's backfield and unstartable. The league roster configuration listed in this context (9 starters + 7 bench) shows no IR slot, in which case he is the second drop, for the Jacksonville DEF stream. IF Sleeper does offer an IR slot for his designation, park him there instead of cutting him - that frees the bench spot for free, and no second drop is needed this week.

waivers.reason: BURN PRIORITY #1 HERE. This is the closest thing in the pool to the league-winner the standing guidance reserves priority for: Sampson is the clear RB2 in Cleveland's run-first offense, and the week Quinshon Judkins misses time he is a bellcow - that is a weekly 15-20 point asset acquired for nothing. 137k trending adds means he does not survive to free agency on Wednesday, and two rivals with RB-hoarding patterns (mrkw, who actually rosters Judkins, and ccharron33) are the exact profile to grab him. Our backfield is Jacobs (bye 11), Harvey (bye 10) and Allgeier, and the Week 10-11 gauntlet also takes Burden (10) and A.J. Brown (11) - we need one more body with starter upside, not a replacement-level warm body. Priority #1 has been held for three weeks with nothing to show for it; its value is zero until it is spent, and at 1-6 the asset we need is RB upside. Mitchell is the drop: no role, no production, no path to one. FALLBACKS if Sampson is claimed ahead of us (we are #1, so this should not happen): Elijah Mitchell (7561) or Austin Ekeler (4663), both takeable in free agency without spending anything.

DO NOT SPEND PRIORITY ON THIS - add in free agency once waivers clear Wednesday, and only if you want the matchup play. Jacksonville is the top trending defense in the pool by a mile (923k adds) with its bye already behind it, which is the market telling us the unit and/or the Week 8 matchup is live; our philosophy is to stream DEF by matchup rather than hold season-long. I could not verify this week's specific opponent before my search budget ran out, so treat this as conditional: if the Jaguars draw a turnover-prone or backup-quarterback offense, start them over Cleveland; if the matchup is neutral, skip the add entirely and keep the roster spot. The drop is Bigsby - BUT see the bench note: if Sleeper offers an IR slot for his designation, park him there instead and this add costs us nothing at all. A secondary benefit is that Jacksonville covers Cleveland's Week 11 bye if we keep both.

get: or Alvin Kamara plus Keon Coleman
trades.pitch: You're 4-3 with seven running backs and five receivers, and Davante Adams is on IR while Drake London is questionable - you're starting Keon Coleman or DeMario Douglas in a slot that should be winning you games, and you have three backs rotting on your bench every Sunday. I'll send you Jameson Williams, who just put up 26.1 and is Detroit's starting field-stretcher, plus Isaiah Likely, who has gone 23.9 and 32.4 in his last two full games as the Giants' every-down tight end. I'd like Jahmyr Gibbs back. If Gibbs is untouchable, I'll do the same package for Alvin Kamara plus Keon Coleman. You already have Brock Bowers, so Likely is either pure trade capital or the only real insurance you have at the one position where you're one injury from nothing - and you fix your receiver room without touching your top backs.
trades.why_it_helps_me: This is the 2-for-1 consolidation the standing guidance asks for: two startable-but-replaceable pieces become a true weekly RB1 at the thinnest position on my roster. Oronde Gadsden covers the TE slot (he is already starting there this week with Likely on bye), and Jefferson, Burden, A.J. Brown and Brian Thomas still fill the receiver spots. At 1-6 I need one dominant asset more than three good ones, and Gibbs is a 20-point weekly swing in the Weeks 14-17 window that is the only window that matters.
trades.why_they_might_accept: Seven backs and a receiver room with one player on IR and another questionable - they are leaving points on their bench every week while starting replacement-level receivers. A one-TE roster taking back the hottest tight end in the league plus a starting WR is a genuine roster-shape fix for a team trying to climb from 4-3 into a first-round bye.

trades.pitch: You're 3-4 and running Kirk Cousins out there as your only quarterback - that's the biggest weekly points gap on your roster and you have zero insurance behind him. I'll send you Lamar Jackson, a two-time MVP who is off the ankle injury and tracking toward a return in the next week or two, so you'd have him for your entire playoff run at a price you could never pay for him healthy, plus Tyler Allgeier as backfield cover with Jeremiyah Love out. I'd like Omarion Hampton back. You get the single biggest positional upgrade available in this league for the weeks that decide your season, you replace the back you're moving, and Garrett Wilson and Jaxon Smith-Njigba never get touched.
trades.why_it_helps_me: Herbert is my starting quarterback right now and has no bye left, so Lamar is a luxury asset I cannot play - converting him into a three-down lead back is exactly the buy-low/sell-injured arbitrage the guidance calls for, just from the sell side. Hampton is a plug-and-play RB1 with his bye already behind him, which solves my Week 10-11 gauntlet and my Weeks 14-17 lineup in one move. NOTE: this is mutually exclusive with the mrkw deal on the Allgeier side - if mrkw accepts first, substitute Brian Thomas Jr. for Allgeier here.
trades.why_they_might_accept: They roster exactly one quarterback and it's Kirk Cousins. A team two games out of the playoff line does not win a title there, and they have receiver surplus but no QB depth at all. Buying an MVP quarterback at an injury discount, with the return date landing before the fantasy playoffs, is the best value swing on their board.

trades.pitch: You're 4-3 with seven running backs and four receivers, and Rashee Rice is out - you physically cannot fill two WR slots with startable players while you sit multiple backs every week. I'll send you two first-round-pedigree receivers: A.J. Brown, a genuine alpha who is off IR and back on the field in New England, plus Brian Thomas Jr., who is a year removed from a 1,000-yard rookie season and a buy-low at his absolute floor. I'd like Quinshon Judkins back; if he's off limits, I'll do the same package for Chuba Hubbard. You turn your two worst starting slots into real receivers and still roster McCaffrey, Warren, Hubbard and Aaron Jones.
trades.why_it_helps_me: Converts two receivers I am not starting - Brown is behind Jefferson, Burden and Jameson Williams and Thomas has back-to-back zeros with a depth-3 role - into a workhorse back at the position where my roster is thinnest. Judkins is a three-down lead back with goal-line work; even Hubbard is a weekly RB2 who outscores my current RB3. My byes (Harvey 10, Jacobs 11) make this the difference between fielding a real lineup in Weeks 10-11 and punting two games.
trades.why_they_might_accept: Four receivers, one of them ruled out, against a seven-deep backfield - the positional math makes this close to free for them. They give up their third or fourth back and get the best player in the deal in A.J. Brown plus a lottery ticket with legitimate WR1 upside if Jacksonville's target distribution ever settles.

confidence_notes: Highest confidence: Herbert at QB (this is the non-negotiable fix - Lamar has missed three straight and the last three packets have eaten a QB zero), Jefferson and Burden as auto-starts, Jacobs restored to the starting backfield after his 20.1, and Dicker back from the bye. Everything in the starting nine has a game and no designation, which is the first time that has been true in a month. Least certain, in order: (1) ORONDE GADSDEN at TE - forced by Likely's bye and a legitimately volatile profile; he has a strong route share but has posted a zero on a sub-9% target share this season, and there is no alternative on the roster, so this slot is simply high-variance. (2) RJ HARVEY - at least one industry outlook has him as a must-sit on matchup grounds this week; I am overriding that on ceiling grounds as a 1-6 underdog, but if Allgeier's matchup is demonstrably elite and Harvey's opponent is a top-five run defense, swapping them is defensible. (3) THE DEFENSE - my live-search budget was exhausted before I could verify the Cleveland or Jacksonville Week 8 game environments, so the CLE hold is the least-researched call in the packet; the Jacksonville add is written as conditional for exactly that reason and is low-leverage either way. (4) A.J. BROWN's practice status this week is unverified - if he is a confirmed full participant with a full route share and Jameson Williams picks up any designation, Brown takes the FLEX. News that changes this packet before kickoff: Lamar cleared to full practice (push the chacetheace48 trade immediately, do not start him over Herbert), Judkins ruled out in Cleveland (Sampson becomes a Week 8 FLEX candidate and the priority spend is a steal), Gadsden ruled out or limited (we would have no healthy TE and would need a Wednesday free-agent add - Hunter Henry (3214) or Mason Taylor (12498) are the fallbacks), or a Sleeper IR slot opening for Bigsby (park him, skip the second drop). Strategic note: at 1-6 the title path requires roughly 6-0 the rest of the way, so every call here is still made for championship equity, not for avoiding last place - but our raw talent (Jefferson, Herbert, Jacobs, Lamar, Likely) is top-half in this league and the points-for deficit is largely self-inflicted lineup error, which is fixable this week.
